He played [[college basketball]] for [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]]. ==High school career== Johnson is the son of Robert Johnson, who played basketball at [[La Salle University]] from 1986 to 1990. The younger Johnson grew up outside Philadelphia and attended [[Lower Merion High School]], [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|NBA Hall-of-Famer]] [[Kobe Bryant]]'s alma mater.{{cite news|last=Waters|first=Mike|title=B.J. Johnson's father details the reasons behind transferring from Syracuse to La Salle|url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2015/03/bj_johnsons_father_details_the_reasons_behind_transferring_from_syracuse_to_lasa.html|accessdate=July 10, 2018|work=[[The Post-Standard]]|date=March 23, 2015}} He had 22 points and 11 rebounds in a win over [[Chester High School (Chester, Pennsylvania)|Chester High School]] in the 2013 state championship. Johnson was a top-100 high school prospect.{{cite news|last=Zeitlin|first=Dave|title=After returning home, B.J. Johnson creating his own legacy at La Salle|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/ncaa/after-returning-home-bj-johnson-creating-his-own-legacy-la-salle|accessdate=July 10, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=December 25, 2016}} ==College career== Johnson originally committed to [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] out of high school. He averaged 4.1 points and 3.1 rebounds per game for the Orange as a sophomore in [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15]]. After the season, he decided to transfer to [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]]. He explained that coach [[John Giannini]] told him he would be an impact player after sitting out the requisite year. Johnson scored 35 points in a December 2016 win over [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast]]. As a junior at La Salle, Johnson led the team in points (17.6 per game) and rebounds (6.3) per game. He was named to the All-[[Philadelphia Big 5|Big 5]] first team. After the season he declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]], but ultimately withdrew his name.{{cite news |title=La Salle's B.J. Johnson will return for senior season |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/la-salle-explorers/la-salles-bj-johnson-will-return-senior-season |accessdate=July 10, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=April 15, 2017}} As a senior, Johnson was named to the All-[[Atlantic 10]] second team.{{cite press release |url=https://atlantic10.com/news/2018/3/6/211704410.aspx |title=Aldridge, Adams Named Atlantic 10 Co-Players of Year, Rhode Island's Hurley Voted as Coach of the Year |publisher=Atlantic 10 Conference |date=March 6, 2018 |access-date=December 6, 2023}} He was also named to the All-Big 5 first team after a season in which he averaged 20.8 points per game, the most for an Explorer since [[Rasual Butler]] in 2002, as well as leading the team with 8.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Johnson Claims Three Philadelphia Big 5 Awards, Including First Team Honors |url=https://goexplorers.com/news/2018/4/11/mens-basketball-johnson-claims-three-philadelphia-big-5-awards-including-first-team-honors.aspx |website=[[La Salle Explorers]] |accessdate=July 10, 2018}} He graduated from La Salle with a degree in finance.{{cite news|last=Hunt|first=Donald|title=La Salle's B.J. Johnson to play for Charlotte Hornets in NBA Summer League |url=http://www.phillytrib.com/sports/la-salle-s-b-j-johnson-to-play-for-charlotte/article_89f5b7fb-a57b-542f-8f14-832ae86618d3.html|accessdate=July 10, 2018 |work=[[The Philadelphia Tribune]]|date=June 25, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Lakeland Magic (2018–2019)=== After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Johnson signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]] for NBA Summer League competition. On September 5, 2018, Johnson signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|title=RELEASE: Magic sign free agent guard B.J. Johnson|url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1037430518059597829|website=Magic PR on Twitter|accessdate=September 5, 2018|date=September 5, 2018}} He was waived by the Magic on October 10 but would play for their [[G League]] affiliate the [[Lakeland Magic]].{{cite news|title=Magic's B.J. Johnson: Waived, will play in G-League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-b-j-johnson-waived-will-play-in-g-league/|accessdate=October 10, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=October 10, 2018}} On October 23, 2018, Johnson was included in Lakeland's training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://lakeland.gleague.nba.com/news/lakeland-magic-finalize-training-camp-roster/|title=LAKELAND MAGIC FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|date=October 23, 2018|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|accessdate=October 23, 2018}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2019)=== On March 1, 2019, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite news |last=Bell |first=N. |date=March 1, 2019 |title=Hawks Sign B.J. Johnson to 10-Day Contract |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/bj-johnson-10-day-contract |accessdate=March 4, 2019}}{{cite news|last=Johnson|first=Parker|title=Johnson ready to make the most of 10-day deal with Hawks|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/basketball/johnson-ready-make-the-most-day-deal-with-hawks/J93rNAsZdltaVeNjF6CUVJ/|accessdate=March 4, 2019|work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|date=March 1, 2019 }} Johnson made his NBA debut two days later, putting up 11 points on perfect 4-of-4 shooting (3-of-3 three-point shooting), 2 rebounds, and a steal during 19 minutes of action in a 123–118 win over the [[2018–19 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web |title=Hawks vs. Bulls - Box Score - March 3, 2019 - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/id/401071619 |website=ESPN.com}} On March 12, Johnson signed a second 10-day contract.{{cite web|title=Hawks' B.J. Johnson: Getting second 10-day contract|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hawks-b-j-johnson-getting-second-10-day-contract/|website=CBS Sports|accessdate=March 24, 2019|date=March 12, 2019}} After the expiration of his second 10-day contract, Johnson returned to the Lakeland Magic. ===Sacramento Kings (2019)=== On April 2, 2019, Johnson signed a rest-of-season contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite news |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=April 2, 2019 |title=Kings Sign B.J. Johnson |work=HoopsRumors.com |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2019/04/kings-sign-b-j-johnson.html |accessdate=December 6, 2023}} On July 19, 2019, Johnson was waived by the Kings.{{cite web |last=Whedbee |first=Alexander |date=July 19, 2019 |title=Kings Waive BJ Johnson |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-bj-johnson |accessdate=July 19, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} ===Orlando Magic (2019–2020)=== [[File:B. J. Johnson and Haywood Highsmith (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Johnson in 2019]] On September 27, 2019, Johnson re-signed with the [[Orlando Magic]] for training camp;{{cite web|title=PRESS RELEASE: Orlando Magic sign free agent B.J. Johnson|url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1177654910516695040|website=Orlando Magic PR on Twitter|accessdate=September 29, 2019|date=September 27, 2019}} however, he was waived on October 19.{{cite web|title=PRESS RELEASE: Magic waive five players|url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1185606598070280201|website=Orlando Magic PR on Twitter|accessdate=November 21, 2019|date=October 19, 2019}} On November 4, the Magic signed him to a two-way contract.{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=November 4, 2019 |title=Magic Sign B.J. Johnson to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-bj-johnson-two-way-contract-20191104 |accessdate=November 21, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} On January 4, 2020, Johnson, playing for Orlando's G League affiliate [[Lakeland Magic]], tallied 35 points, eight rebounds and two assists in the G League against the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite news |title=Magic's B.J. Johnson: Pops off for 35 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-b-j-johnson-pops-off-for-35/ |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 4, 2020}} He averaged 22.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.1 steals per game for Lakeland. Johnson was named to the All-NBA G League Second Team.{{cite web |title=Johnson, Magette and Law Named to All-NBA G League Teams |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/johnson-magette-and-law-named-to-all-nba-g-league-teams/n-5625789 |website=Our Sports Central |accessdate=June 28, 2020 |date=June 26, 2020}} ===Long Island Nets (2021)=== On December 4, 2020, Johnson signed with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web |title=BJ Johnson Signs With HEAT |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/bj-johnson-signs-with-heat-120420 |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=December 4, 2020}} On December 19, 2020, Johnson was waived by the Heat.{{cite web |last=Winderman |first=Ira |date=December 19, 2020 |title=Max Strus earns final Heat roster spot, on two-way deal; guard BJ Johnson waived |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2020/12/19/max-strus-earns-final-heat-roster-spot-on-two-way-deal-guard-bj-johnson-waived |access-date=December 19, 2020 |website=sun-sentinel.com}} He was added to the [[Long Island Nets]] roster and made his debut on February 10, 2021. In 14 games, he averaged 18.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.0 steals in 31.1 minutes per game.{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=December 17, 2021 |title=Orlando Magic Sign Ford, Gravett, Johnson and Schofield to 10-Day Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-ford-gravett-johnson-and-schofield-10-day-contracts-20211217 |access-date=December 17, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} ===Brisbane Bullets (2021)=== On April 19, 2021, Johnson signed with the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] for the remainder of the [[2020–21 NBL season|2020–21 season]].{{cite web|title=Bullets Sign Import BJ Johnson|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bullets-sign-import-bj-johnson|website=NBL.com.au|date=April 19, 2021|access-date=April 19, 2021}} In 11 games, he averaged 10.0 points and 3.7 rebounds in 21.5 minutes per game. ===Second stint with Lakeland / Orlando Magic (2021–2022)=== On October 15, 2021, Johnson signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],{{cite web |last=Brumbelow |first=Brooke |date=October 15, 2021 |title=Orlando Magic Sign B.J. Johnson |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-bj-johnson-20211015 |access-date=October 16, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} but was waived the next day.{{cite web |last=Brumbelow |first=Brooke |date=October 16, 2021 |title=Orlando Magic Waive Four Players |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-waive-four-players-20211016 |access-date=October 17, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} On October 28, he re-signed with the [[Lakeland Magic]] as an affiliate player{{cite web|title=Lakeland Magic 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://lakeland.gleague.nba.com/news/lakeland-magic-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2021|access-date=December 17, 2021}} where he played 10 games and averaged 24.7 points, 7.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.0 steals in 34.5 minutes per game. On December 17, 2021, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with the Orlando Magic. and on January 4, 2022, he was reacquired and activated by Lakeland.{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|date=January 4, 2022|access-date=January 4, 2022}} ===Real Betis (2022–2023)=== On April 6, 2022, Johnson signed with [[Real Betis Baloncesto|Coosur Real Betis]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web |date=April 6, 2022 |title=BJ Johnson, nuevo jugador del Coosur Real Betis |url=https://www.realbetisbalompie.es/noticias/baloncesto/bj-johnson-nuevo-jugador-del-coosur-real-betis-27464 |access-date=April 6, 2022 |website=RealBetisBalompie.es |language=es}} ===Phoenix Super LPG Fuel Masters (2026–present)=== In June 2026, Johnson signed with the [[Phoenix Super LPG Fuel Masters]] as the team's import for the [[2026 PBA Governors' Cup]].{{cite web|last=Joble|first=Rey|url=https://all-starmagazine.com/news-and-updates/bj-johnson-phoenix-fuel-masters/|title=Phoenix pins hopes on NBA/G League Vet BJ Johnson|date=June 16, 2026|accessdate=June
